lead: Anthropic dominates the overnight cycle on three fronts at once: an internal research model that finds and exploits real browser vulnerabilities, a push into drug development with six pharma partners and its first biotech acquisition, and a discounted Claude offering for every level of US government. Apple, Meta's chip suppliers and the coders'-job debate fill out the day.

sections.title: Claude finds the holes
sections.intro: Anthropic's unreleased research model built multi-step exploit chains against Chrome and Safari - 62 CVEs, sandbox escapes, a full same-origin bypass - all under coordinated disclosure as a bellwether for model cyber capability.

sections.title: Claude goes to the lab
sections.intro: Six drug development partnerships, an in-house discovery effort and the acquisition of one-person muscular dystrophy startup Mithril mark Anthropic's most concrete move into medicine.

sections.title: Cupertino's AI week
sections.intro: Creator Studio got its biggest update since launch - MotionVFX in Final Cut Pro, assistants across Logic Pro and the iWork apps, MCP support and an open Keynote format - while Siri AI added five languages, still skipping the EU.

sections.title: The state and the clinic
sections.intro: Anthropic cut Claude prices 40% for US governments as adoption surges, while the EFF's latest records show Medicare's AI prior-authorization rollout was rushed and opaque, and another report puts chatbot medical advice under the microscope.

sections.title: Chips and equity
sections.intro: Nvidia and AMD put $4 billion into Meta's raise with Helios racks already installed, while The Information reports OpenAI plans to buy Google TPUs - a crack in the Nvidia-only era.

sections.title: The developer's new job description
sections.intro: An Anthropic hiring manager retired coding interviews because Claude aces them - 'hunger beats tenure' - and Amazon published its own definition of the developer's durable role in the AI age.

sections.title: Odds and ends
sections.intro: A data study found owners worry about reliability twice as much as reviewers do, and Infisical raised $40 million to keep agent credentials out of agent hands.
